cards.text: Isaiah, the prophet, has another burden, and this one is against Dumah. He says someone calls to him, calling out for the watchman, the one whose whole job is to stay awake and keep guard. Friend, I did that job for YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and nobody ever paid me.

cards.question: In the burden against Dumah, where does that voice calling for the watchman come from?
The voice from Seir calls to the watchman, the one keeping guard while everyone else sleeps. What does it want to know?

answers.text: How much of the night is left
Who is coming up the road
Whether the city is still safe

cards.question: The voice from Seir asks the watchman how much of the night is left only one time.

cards.text: Now the watchman answers. And I know that pressure, friend: when somebody asks you the SAME question twice, you better come back with something good.

cards.question: The watchman's answer is all good news: morning has come and the night is over.

cards.text: Morning has come, but also the night. That's a weather app promising sunshine AND storms in the same hour, and you KNOW I'd still refresh it twice.

cards.question: The watchman doesn't send the caller away. He says if the caller wants to ___, then go ahead, and come back yet again.
